topic: Moving house: lift smarter, not harder

slides.headline: Moving house? Lift smarter, not harder
slides.sub: A back-friendly plan for moving day and the week before it.

slides.title: Pack smaller boxes
slides.body: Heavy items like books go in small boxes, and light things like linen go in big ones. Aim for boxes you can lift comfortably without holding your breath.

slides.title: Warm up before the first load
slides.body: A few minutes of walking, squats and gentle trunk turns prepares your body for a big day. Moving house is a full-body workout, so treat it like one.

slides.title: Keep it close
slides.body: Hold boxes close to your body, bend at the hips and knees, and pivot with your feet rather than twisting. Use a trolley for anything awkward or heavy.

slides.title: Pace the day
slides.body: Take short breaks every hour, drink water and eat properly. Strains often happen when people are tired and rushing the last few loads. Share heavy lifts with a mate.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain spreading down a leg, numbness, weakness, or changes to bladder or bowel control need prompt medical attention. Stiffness that hasn't eased after a week is worth assessing.

slides.headline: Sore after the big move?
slides.body: Our chiropractors assess how you move, then combine hands-on care and exercise to help you settle into the new place. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Moving house is basically a full day of deadlifts, so plan for it like one. 📦

Pack heavy things in small boxes and light things in big ones. Warm up before the first load, keep boxes close to your body and turn with your feet instead of twisting. A trolley and a mate make the awkward items much easier.

Pace yourself too. Strains often happen late in the day when everyone is tired and rushing. Some stiffness afterwards is common, but pain down a leg, numbness or weakness need prompt attention.

If you're still stiff a week later, our chiropractors at Hybrid Physiotherapy can help. Book online via the link in bio.
